subject: Localized range anchors + regional benchmarking request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Park <andrew.park@peopletalent.co>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Localized range anchors + regional benchmarking request

Hi team,

We need to finalize regional anchors for our leveling matrix before the next hiring sprint. People Ops flagged a few offer exceptions last week in Dublin and Lisbon where the US-based band midpoint didn't map cleanly. To avoid repeated ad-hoc uplifts, I propose we: 

- Lock down localized anchor multipliers for EU markets (Dublin, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Berlin) for levels IC3-IC6.
- Run a small probe cohort (6 offers) using the candidate-weighted median from CompBench to validate market tolerance.
- Produce a one-page offer template showing Base / Equity / Sign-on / Locality multiplier and an approval bucket for >10% deviation.

I attached a working spreadsheet (geo-anchor-spreadsheet-v2.xlsx) with my suggested anchors as an initial draft. Ask list for this thread: 
1) Karthik — can you confirm approvals flow for >10% deltas (who signs off for hiring managers vs. compensation)?
2) Laura — please confirm whether headcount approvals change if we adopt local anchors (will FP&A require a reforecast?).
3) Andrew (external People Ops consultant) — can CompBench deliver a short benchmark summary by EOD Monday for the four markets above?

Goal: have anchors defined and a pilot offer bundle ready by the end of next week so Talent can field offers consistently.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of People Analytics
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: geo-anchor-spreadsheet-v2.xlsx (sheet: proposed-multipliers)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Localized range anchors + regional benchmarking request

Thanks Jonas — this looks actionable. A few clarifying points: 

1) Approvals: Compensation exceptions up to +/-10% remain within Talent/Comp sign-off. Anything above 10% requires manager + me + finance (Laura) approval. For sign-ons >20% we escalate to VP People.

2) Headcount: If we adopt localized anchors and the midpoint shifts cause >5% uplift to total comp for an open headcount bucket, FP&A wants a reforecast. Laura, can you confirm the 5% threshold and whether we can treat the probe cohort as neutral for this calculation?

3) Probe cohort: I support 6 offers but prefer we pick two senior (IC5) and four mid (IC3–IC4) roles to stress test. Also recommend we include one contract conversion on the cohort.

If Laura and Andrew are good with timeline, I'll put an approvals checklist for managers and create a stub PRD for the pilot so Talent has a single source of truth.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Recruiting & Compensation
Redwood Inference

From: CompBench Benchmarking <bench@compbench.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Andrew Park <andrew.park@peopletalent.co>
Date: 2027-05-17T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Localized range anchors + regional benchmarking request

Hi Jonas / Andrew,

Attached is a rapid summary for Dublin, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Berlin for IC3–IC6 (compbench-report-summary.pdf). High-level findings: 

- Market index multipliers (vs US national midpoint): Dublin 1.08, Amsterdam 1.00, Berlin 0.94, Lisbon 0.82.
- Candidate-weighted median base differs from job-weighted median by ~3–4% in Dublin and Amsterdam (senior technical roles skew higher).
- Recommended anchor approach: keep our band slopes identical, apply a location multiplier to midpoints, and add a 5% local market uplift band for high-demand roles (subject to approval).

Deliverables we can provide by Thursday if you confirm: full breakdown by job family, comp-ratio charts, and a short memo explaining the methodology.

Quick request: provide the final list of job families and exact titles for the probe cohort so we can produce job-matched medians.

Regards,
CompBench Team
CompBench Benchmarking

Attachment: compbench-report-summary.pdf
Link: https://compbench.com/reports/RI-2027-EU-index

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: CompBench Benchmarking <bench@compbench.com>, Andrew Park <andrew.park@peopletalent.co>
Date: 2027-05-17T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Localized range anchors + regional benchmarking request

Thanks all — good momentum. Summary & next steps: 

- CompBench delivered the index multipliers (attached). I agree with the multiplier approach rather than rewriting slopes.
- Karthik: we'll select the probe cohort two IC5s + four IC3–IC4s; I'll drop job families into the shared Drive by EOD.
- Laura: please confirm FP&A tolerance on the 5% reforecast threshold — if confirmed, we'll mark the probe cohort as exempt for reforecasting so we can move quickly.
- Deliverables: CompBench to provide job-family matched medians and a one-page methodology memo by Thursday.

Approvals checklist (to be finalized by Karthik): 
- Manager: initial offer ok
- Talent/Comp (Karthik): anchor multiplier applied
- Finance (Laura): sign-off if uplift causes >5% spend delta
- VP People: only if sign-on >20% or recurring uplift >15% for a role band

I'll update the sheet and publish a short offer template (Base / Equity / Sign-on / Locality multiplier / Approvals) in Drive. If everyone is aligned, we can start sending pilot offers on Monday next week.
